digest.component_or_area: completion verifier budget and caching (completion.py, completion_recovery.py, completion_banking.py)
propositions: Verifier step budget exhausts on legitimate multi-criterion validation (e.g. epic tickets with 6-15 criteria), marking valid criteria as unmet when only out-of-budget rather than actually unprovable.

Current budget formula (steps_per_criterion × count, clamped at 480) lacks evidence-surface scaling for ticket-graph traversal (child show_ticket, comments, repo reads per child), causing underestimation for epics.
Re-verification after budget exhaustion re-proves all criteria from scratch instead of crediting previously validated PASS verdicts, driving 10-minute retry cycles and operator attestation pressure.

A cross-run PASS-verdict cache keyed by criterion-text hash and scoped content fingerprint (git blob SHAs of file_impact paths) enables seeding of still-valid verdicts into the run bank, bypassing re-verification while detecting invalidation on file or criterion text changes.

Budget defaults must scale from 8→24 steps/criterion and 48→160 floor-min with a new child-traversal term (16 steps per direct child, 16 fixed overhead) so 6-AC epics size to ≥80 requests and 15-AC epics to ≥180, with clamp raised from 480 to 960 to prevent false-limiting authorized validation.

Runaway protection (tool_calls_limit, loop detection, hard clamp) is orthogonal; a small budget adds no runaway safety but only false failures, so budget is re-framed as a generous floor with child-aware scaling, never an artificial validation cap.
